title: Senior+ Software Engineer, Legal Tech
location: Remote-Friendly (Travel-Required) | San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA | New York City, NY
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Legal Tech engineers play a specialized and critical role in keeping Claude at the frontier. Partnering closely with counsel, we provide custom infrastructure and guidance for complex, novel technical matters, empowering teams across the company to continue meeting our legal obligations as we innovate.

As a Senior+ Software Engineer on our Legal Tech team, you'll build dedicated, highly secure, and reliable cloud environments and data processing and storage capabilities at speed and scale. You will own your scope end to end: from raw requirements all the way through to large-scale production systems that satisfy legal invariants and unlock new possibilities. The systems you build won't just be dependable and scalable; they'll be interpretable and auditable, demonstrating to skeptical audiences exactly how they worked and why results can be trusted.

You'll be an essential member of a collaborative team, working together to solve difficult problems against fixed deadlines. You will own internal customer relationships as well: you'll gather, prioritize, and coordinate needs from colleagues on Privacy, Security, Research, and/or Infra as well as Legal, to ship the right capabilities on the right timelines. You'll act as a trusted advisor: clearly explaining technical concepts and constraints to inform legal decisions, and proactively designing new approaches to prevent classes of problems. Your infrastructure expertise will directly empower our business to calibrate and manage risk, innovating faster thanks to systems that build in legal considerations.

Key responsibilities

  • Build and operate dedicated cloud infrastructure, storage, and data pipelines for specialized workloads that can't run on general-purpose systems

  • Design architectures with excellent security, privacy, reliability, scalability, and auditability baked in

  • Partner with a wide range of internal customer teams to translate requirements into sound approaches and realistic ETAs

  • Deliver against fixed deadlines

  • Support complex and novel legal requests on controlled infrastructure, with verifiable chain of custody

  • Pair with engineering teams across the company to extend existing infrastructure to support new workflows and/or legal requests

  • Work with nontechnical stakeholders to clarify their needs through responsive, easy-to-follow dialogue

Minimum qualifications

  • Experience designing, building, and operating highly trusted infrastructure and data systems in production, including owning architectural decisions

  • Experience working across large, complex, multi-team environments, including in stacks and code you don't own

  • Ability to take ownership of a cloud account and secure it end to end (networking, storage, identity, encryption, least-privilege provisioning, etc.) on AWS and/or GCP

  • Ability to translate legal and privacy requirements into sound technical designs and implementations that teams are excited to adopt

  • A habit of verifying rather than assuming: designing checks for invariants and plainly naming what isn't proved

  • Self-directed in a high-change environment, and comfortable resequencing quickly when new needs emerge

  • Clear communication with nontechnical stakeholders, and an understanding of their needs

Preferred qualifications

  • Software engineering experience with an infrastructure, data, privacy, and/or security focus

  • Proficiency with large-scale data tooling, such as distributed processing, lakehouse table formats, and/or query engines

  • Understanding of data processing pipelines, LLM training, and/or provenance and lineage

  • Experience with secure enclaves, confidential computing, clean rooms, or other purpose-built environments for sensitive data

  • Background in eDiscovery, litigation support, or records retention at scale, including chain of custody and verifiable integrity

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$320,000—$485,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

title: Fuel System Superintendent
description:
The Fuel System Superintendent provides onsite leadership for fuel-system construction projects, with primary responsibility for the safe, timely, and quality installation of fuel storage tanks, piping, electrical systems, controls, monitoring equipment, and related project materials.


The Superintendent determines daily field priorities based on the project schedule, approved drawings, project requirements, management direction, and customer needs. This position directly supervises JF Petroleum Group field employees and coordinates onsite subcontractors, vendors, testing agencies, and startup representatives.


The position may oversee underground storage tank and aboveground storage tank installations and the mechanical, electrical, controls, and related systems directly associated with the fuel system. The Superintendent works closely with the Project Manager, who retains responsibility for contract administration, project financial management, and formal change-order processing.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities:


Field Supervision and Coordination

· Provide direct daily supervision of JF Petroleum Group field employees and onsite subcontractors.

· Supervise the installation of fuel storage tanks, piping systems, electrical systems, controls, monitoring equipment, and related project materials.

· Coordinate underground and aboveground fuel-system installation activities as required by the project.

· Determine daily work priorities based on the project schedule, approved drawings, available materials, site conditions, management direction, and customer requirements.

· Communicate daily work requirements, safety expectations, and installation priorities to employees and subcontractors.

· Coordinate petroleum installers, electricians, equipment operators, subcontractors, vendors, testing agencies, and startup technicians.

· Coordinate with the Project Manager, customer, general contractor, and other onsite representatives regarding project progress, site conditions, inspections, scheduling, and issues affecting the work.

· Maintain professional communication with customers, contractors, inspectors, and project stakeholders.

· Identify drawing conflicts, field conditions, missing information, or potential delays and report them promptly to the Project Manager.

· Do not direct or perform work outside the approved project scope without authorization from the Project Manager.

· Direct and coordinate the daily work of assigned field employees and subcontractors.

· Provide clear instructions, coaching, training, and performance feedback.

· Monitor attendance, work quality, productivity, safety compliance, and professional conduct.

· Review employee timecards for accuracy and verify time is assigned to the correct project and work activity.

· Notify the appropriate manager of employee performance, attendance, safety, or conduct concerns.

· Promote accountability, teamwork, respect, and professional conduct on the job site.

Fuel System Installation

· Supervise tank installation activities, including excavation coordination, bedding, tank placement, anchoring, piping, containment systems, backfill, equipment installation, and startup.

· Coordinate crane access, tank unloading, rigging, lifting, and tank-setting activities.

· Verify tanks, piping, equipment, and related materials are installed according to approved drawings, specifications, manufacturer instructions, and project requirements.

· Supervise installation of fuel-product piping, vent piping, fill piping, suction or pressure piping, day-tank piping, and related fuel-system components.

· Verify proper installation of pumps, valves, leak-detection equipment, tank-monitoring systems, sensors, emergency shutdowns, fuel controls, and related equipment.

· Coordinate electrical power, conduit, wiring, controls, grounding, bonding, equipment connections, and emergency-shutdown requirements associated with the fuel system.

· Confirm fuel-system components are compatible with the product stored and the approved project design.

· Protect tanks, piping, coatings, electrical components, controls, and equipment from damage during construction.

· Confirm underground systems are properly documented and inspected before they are covered or backfilled.

Plans Specifications and Code Compliance

· Read and understand applicable drawings, specifications, approved submittals, equipment schedules, wiring diagrams, control diagrams, and manufacturer instructions.

· Verify field installation work follows the current approved construction documents.

· Maintain current drawings onsite and clearly identify field changes for record-drawing and as-built purposes.

· Understand and enforce applicable environmental regulations and fire, building, electrical, and fuel-system requirements.

· Coordinate questions or conflicts involving drawings, specifications, or installation requirements with the Project Manager.

· Participate in inspections with fire, building, electrical, environmental, or other regulatory authorities as required.

Scheduling and Meetings

· Assist in developing, maintaining, and communicating the project schedule.

· Prepare short-term work plans for employees, subcontractors, equipment, materials, inspections, testing, and startup activities.

· Monitor daily progress and promptly report conditions that may affect the project schedule.

· Lead or participate in preconstruction, daily pre-task planning, safety, progress, coordination, inspection, testing, commissioning, and project closeout meetings as applicable.

Quality Control Testing and Commissioning

· Monitor installation quality and correct deficient or incomplete work before systems are covered, backfilled, energized, or placed into service.

· Verify required tests and inspections are completed and documented.

· Coordinate applicable tank, piping, containment, electrical, controls, monitoring, sensor, emergency-shutdown, and operational testing.

· Coordinate with testing contractors, electricians, equipment manufacturers, startup technicians, inspectors, and commissioning representatives.

· Track inspection deficiencies and punch-list items through completion.

· Assist with system startup, commissioning, owner training, and final turnover.

· Confirm tanks, piping, valves, panels, controls, fill points, and emergency equipment are properly labeled and identified.

Project Documentation

· Maintain accurate daily project records.

· Document employees and subcontractors onsite, work completed, equipment used, deliveries, testing, inspections, safety activities, visitors, delays, changed conditions, schedule impacts, and issues requiring Project Manager follow-up.

· Maintain clear photographs of daily progress, underground installations, equipment identification, testing, inspections, and completed work.

· Maintain inspection reports, test results, delivery tickets, startup reports, and other required project records.

· Use Procore or other company-approved systems for daily reports, photographs, drawings, RFIs, inspections, observations, and punch-list documentation.

· Assist the Project Manager with as-built information, testing records, equipment documentation, warranties, and project closeout requirements.

Performance Expectations

· Safe execution of field activities.

· Effective supervision of employees and subcontractors.

· Compliance with approved drawings, specifications, codes, and manufacturer requirements.

· Achievement of project schedule milestones and delivery of complete, high-quality fuel systems.

· Timely and accurate daily documentation.

· Effective communication with the Project Manager, customer, and project team.

· Successful completion of inspections, testing, startup, commissioning, and turnover.

· Professional conduct and customer service.

Safety Requirements

· Lead and enforce all company safety policies and procedures.

· Conduct a Job Safety Analysis and pre-task safety discussion with the crew before beginning work.

· Supervise the daily activities of employees, subcontractors, vendors, and material suppliers onsite.

· Identify potential hazards and require corrective action.

· Require proper personal protective equipment for all employees and subcontractors.

· Conduct or participate in required weekly jobsite safety meetings.

· Ensure employees and subcontractors receive and follow required project-specific safety training.

· Enforce excavation, trenching, fall-protection, confined-space, lockout/tagout, hot-work, utility-location, and equipment-safety requirements as applicable.

· Serve as the designated competent person only when properly trained, qualified, and assigned.

· Stop work when an unsafe condition presents an immediate risk to employees, the public, the environment, equipment, or property.

· Immediately report incidents, injuries, near misses, spills, utility strikes, equipment damage, and property damage.

· Maintain good housekeeping and ensure the work area remains organized and safe.

Physical and General Work Expectations

· Work outdoors and indoors in varying temperatures and weather conditions.

· Walk active construction sites and work around excavations, heavy equipment, cranes, traffic, fuel systems, and electrical equipment.

· Climb ladders, bend, kneel, and stand for extended periods.

· Access confined or restricted areas when properly trained and authorized.

· Lift and carry materials or equipment consistent with company policy and applicable safety requirements.

· Wear required personal protective equipment.

· Work nights, weekends, extended hours, or scheduled shutdown periods when required.

· Travel and stay overnight near assigned project locations as required.

title: Head of Product
description:
Head of Product

Full-Time | Leadership Position

Build a product experience that changes how trade businesses run.

At Profitable Tradie, we’re not here to deliver more content for the sake of it. We’re here to help trade business owners build better businesses and create more Time, Money and Freedom.

We’re looking for a Head of Product who can turn that promise into an exceptional member experience - and build a team that delivers it consistently.

Someone who can see the bigger picture, set a clear direction, bring out the best in people and make sure the work we put into the world genuinely makes a difference.

Who We Are

Profitable Tradie helps trade business owners across New Zealand, Australia and North America build more profitable, better-run businesses.

Through coaching, education, events, tools and resources, we help our members take control of their businesses and create a better life.

And we’re growing. Which means we need a Product leader who can keep raising the bar on what we deliver and how we deliver it.

What You’ll Be Doing

You’ll lead the strategy, people and performance of our Product Department - bringing together curriculum, training, events, resources, video, member experience and partnerships into one connected, high-quality offering.

You’ll set the direction, decide what matters most and turn company strategy into clear priorities, with the right people accountable for delivering them.

You’ll build a high-performing team that takes ownership, delivers on its commitments and produces work it’s proud of. That means coaching people to grow, setting clear expectations and addressing performance when it falls short.

You’ll also own the standard of the member experience. From the quality of our training to the way our events and resources help members take action, you’ll make sure what we deliver is practical, relevant and genuinely valuable.

And you’ll keep asking the question that matters most: Is this helping our members get better results?

Working closely with Coaching, Marketing, Sales, Operations and the Executive Team, you’ll use member feedback, data and commercial insight to keep improving our offering and contributing to PT’s growth.

Who You Are

You’re a strategic leader who knows how to turn a big-picture vision into consistent results.

You lead through others. You set clear expectations, give honest feedback, develop great people and hold your team accountable without micromanaging or stepping in to do everyone’s job.

You have a sharp eye for quality and know the difference between work that’s simply finished and work that’s genuinely excellent.

You’re commercially minded. You understand that great Product isn’t just about creating a brilliant experience - it’s about delivering real value for members and helping the business grow.

You’re decisive, organised and comfortable making tough calls. You can prioritise what matters, build systems that make quality repeatable and keep things moving without needing someone to chase you.

Most importantly, you care about outcomes. You want to know whether members are getting better results, whether your team is thriving and whether the department is making a meaningful contribution to the business.

Why Join Us?

This is an opportunity to shape the experience of thousands of trade business owners and help build a Product function that can grow with PT.

You’ll have the scope to set the direction, build a capable team and make meaningful improvements to the way we serve our members.

You’ll work alongside a leadership team that cares about results, values ownership and wants to keep getting better.

And you’ll have the chance to help create something that matters - for our members, our people and the future of Profitable Tradie.

Is This Your Moment?

If you’re ready to lead a team, raise the standard and build a Product experience that delivers real results, we’d love to hear from you.

Life is about moments. The ones where you step up, take ownership and make a bigger impact.

Is this your moment? – Apply Now!

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer, Client Platform
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Full Stack Engineer, Client Platform based in United States .

This is a senior full-stack engineering role focused on enabling product teams to build and deliver high-quality digital experiences efficiently. The role combines React and TypeScript development with backend GraphQL engineering and API design.   • Manage GraphQL schemas as versioned contracts, identifying breaking changes, coordinating migrations across client teams, and keeping generated client models synchronized.
  • Develop, scale, and optimize GraphQL APIs, RPC endpoints, and SQL queries supporting digital client experiences.
  • Build front-end applications and shared component libraries using React and TypeScript, with a strong focus on performance and accessibility.
  • Partner with product and design teams to architect and deliver customer-facing features end-to-end.
  • Use observability tools to diagnose production issues, improve user experiences, and establish effective monitoring and alerting through Datadog.
  • Identify technical debt, production bottlenecks, scalability risks, and opportunities to improve code quality and platform performance.
  • Contribute to system design, architecture, feature delivery, and technical standards within a collaborative Agile environment.
  • Develop comprehensive automated tests for new features and bug fixes, working with QA to strengthen testing pipelines and CI/CD workflows.
  • Mentor engineers through code reviews, pairing, documentation, and knowledge sharing.
  • Incorporate agentic development tools such as Claude Code into daily engineering workflows while maintaining strong quality standards.

    • Requirements:

    • At least 5 years of professional software engineering experience.
    • Strong JavaScript, TypeScript, and React skills, combined with solid UX instincts.
    • At least 2 years of experience designing and evolving GraphQL schemas for product surfaces used across multiple clients, including iOS, Android, and web.
    • Strong knowledge of HTML, CSS, and browser technologies, including the DOM, events, and platform APIs.
    • Solid computer science fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, distributed systems, and software design.
    • Experience working with production systems at scale, including load testing, tracing, performance analysis, and optimization.
    • Experience investigating and resolving production performance regressions, including CPU hotspots and latency issues in high-throughput services.
    • Experience participating in on-call rotations and owning production release cycles end-to-end.
    • Strong focus on clean architecture, maintainable code, and software craftsmanship.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience producing technical specifications, runbooks, and cross-team design documentation.

    • Experience with Kubernetes and operating services in containerized environments.
    • Comfortable working with terminal-based development tools, Git, GitHub or similar platforms, and modern code editors.
    • Experience with testing frameworks such as Jest, Vitest, ExUnit, RSpec, or pytest.
    • Experience with Apollo Federation at scale or GraphQL APIs using Absinthe is a plus.
    • Mobile development experience with Swift or Kotlin, as well as knowledge of relational databases such as PostgreSQL and MySQL, is desirable.

    • Passion for sports or esports is considered an advantage.

title: Analista de Riscos e Controles de Segurança da Informação Sênior
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Analista de Riscos e Controles de Segurança da Informação Sênior based in Brazil.

As a Senior Information Security Risk and Controls Analyst, you will play a key role in identifying, assessing, and treating information security risks across the organization. You will help strengthen security controls, evaluate their effectiveness, and drive remediation initiatives through to completion. The role also includes third-party risk management, security maturity assessments, and governance activities. You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Cloud, Compliance, and Legal teams to embed security and risk management into projects from the beginning. Your ability to investigate complex scenarios and translate technical risks into clear recommendations will support both operational and executive decision-making. This is a highly autonomous role in a collaborative, agile environment where technical expertise and attention to detail are valued.

Accountabilities:

  • Lead the end-to-end information security risk management lifecycle, including risk identification, analysis, evaluation, and treatment in accordance with ISO/IEC 27005.
  • Apply and continuously improve risk management methodologies, including qualitative probability-versus-impact matrices and, where appropriate, quantitative approaches such as FAIR.
  • Define and monitor risk treatment plans covering mitigation, transfer, acceptance, or avoidance, ensuring appropriate follow-up through formal closure or acceptance.
  • Maintain and test the information security controls framework, assessing control effectiveness, documenting exceptions, and monitoring corrective action plans.
  • Conduct security control maturity assessments and gap analyses based on frameworks such as ISO/IEC 27001/27002, NIST CSF, and CIS Controls.
  • Lead third-party and supplier risk assessments, including due diligence, criticality classification, and monitoring of contractual security requirements.
  • Develop and maintain risk and control indicators, including KRIs and KPIs, and prepare technical and executive-level reports to support decision-making.
  • Act as a technical advisor to Product, Engineering, Cloud, Compliance, and Legal teams, promoting security-by-design and risk mitigation throughout project development.
  • Support formal risk acceptance and exception management processes through appropriate documentation, governance, and periodic reviews.

    • Requirements:

    • Proven professional experience in information security risk management.
    • Strong practical and in-depth knowledge of ISO/IEC 27005, including risk identification, analysis, evaluation, probability and impact criteria, and treatment planning.
    • Solid understanding of ISO/IEC 27001/27002, NIST CSF, and CIS Controls and their relationship to information security risk management.
    • Experience with third-party risk management (TPRM), including supplier due diligence, criticality assessments, and contractual security requirements.
    • Demonstrated ability to design and perform control effectiveness testing, manage supporting evidence, and track remediation plans through completion.
    • Strong technical writing and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex security risks into clear language for executive and business audiences.
    • Strong organization, autonomy, analytical thinking, and senior-level judgment when handling complex assessments with limited supervision.
    • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional background in information security, technology, risk management, or a related field is desirable.
    • Certifications such as ISO 27005 Risk Manager, CRISC, or ISO 27001 Lead Implementer/Auditor are desirable.
    • Experience with quantitative risk modeling, such as FAIR or equivalent methodologies, is a plus.
    • Experience in regulated environments, particularly financial or payment institutions subject to Central Bank of Brazil regulations, is a plus.
    • Ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical security and risk management processes is desirable.

title: Security Analyst
description:
Start Your Adventure at Via Logic

Location: Onsite at a government site in the Washington, DC metropolitan area
Type: Full-time, W-2
Compensation: $80,000–$130,000 annually, depending on experience and assignment
Experience: Approximately 1–5 years of relevant experience; we are considering candidates across multiple experience levels

Eligibility & Clearance Requirements

Due to CBP contract requirements, applicants must:

  • Be a U.S. citizen.
  • Meet CBP suitability requirements for access to government facilities and systems.
  • Meet any clearance requirements for the specific assignment. Some openings may require a Secret or Top Secret clearance; certain specialized assignments may also require SCI eligibility. We will confirm the requirement for each role.

One posting, several possible routes. We are hiring for multiple openings at different experience levels, which is why the experience and salary ranges are broad. Depending on the assignment, you could work in security monitoring, threat analysis, incident response, investigations, or vulnerability assessment. We will match your strengths to the role that fits.

Your Mission

  • Analyze security alerts, logs, events, and other data to identify suspicious activity and assess its impact.
  • Investigate potential incidents, document findings, and help teams determine appropriate escalation and response.
  • Support vulnerability analysis, threat intelligence, or proactive threat hunting where aligned with your skills.
  • Collaborate with engineers, incident responders, system owners, and other stakeholders to resolve findings and strengthen defenses.
  • Maintain clear case notes, reports, procedures, and recommendations that others can act on.

What You Bring to the Expedition

  • Approximately 1–5 years of experience in security operations, cyber analysis, incident response, investigations, vulnerability assessment, or a related discipline.
  • Experience interpreting alerts and logs, researching potential threats, and explaining findings clearly.
  • Familiarity with security monitoring or investigation tools, such as SIEM, endpoint detection, vulnerability scanning, or threat intelligence platforms.
  • Sound judgment about when to investigate further, escalate, or involve another technical team.
  • Ability to work onsite in the Washington, DC metropolitan area.

Experience with detection rules, network traffic analysis, digital evidence, insider threat monitoring, or penetration testing is welcome. We will match candidates to openings based on the depth of their experience in those areas.

Your Route Into Via Logic

We are hiring across several openings and experience levels through this posting. Tell us which security disciplines you have worked in, the tools you have used, and your current clearance status so we can identify the best fit.

Why Explorers Stay

  • Healthcare coverage and paid time off that give you room to take care of life outside work.
  • Teammates who share knowledge, pitch in, and help each other grow.
  • Opportunities to deepen your specialty and explore adjacent areas of cybersecurity as new assignments open up.
  • Meaningful work protecting systems that support a federal mission.

How We Work

  • These positions work onsite at a government site in the Washington, DC metropolitan area. The specific site depends on the assignment.
  • You’ll collaborate with Via Logic teammates, government partners, and other technical teams using tools approved for your work environment.
  • Schedules depend on the assignment. Some teams work daytime Eastern Time hours; others may have shift or on-call requirements. We’ll discuss the schedule for a specific opening before moving forward.
  • When virtual meetings are part of the work, we expect active participation and use video when appropriate and permitted by the client environment.

About Via Logic

Via Logic LLC is an information technology partner supporting mission-driven work across DevSecOps, cloud engineering, cybersecurity, data science, and national security analytics for federal and commercial clients. Our teams help modernize complex systems through automation, secure engineering practices, cloud-native technologies, and scalable infrastructure solutions that support real-world impact. But beyond the work itself, we care deeply about how we work. We believe great teams are built through collaboration, curiosity, accountability, and trust. Whether you're supporting customer missions, strengthening business operations, or leading expeditions of your own, Via Logic is a place where Explorers are encouraged to grow, contribute, and continuously evolve.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Via Logic LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace where all Explorers are valued and supported. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable federal, state, or local law. We believe different perspectives strengthen teams, improve innovation, and help us build better solutions for the missions we support.

Accessibility & Accommodations

Via Logic is committed to providing an accessible and inclusive hiring experience for all candidates. Reasonable accommodations are available throughout the application and interview process to support accessibility needs and ensure every candidate has an equitable opportunity to explore a career with our team.

Recruiting Fraud Notice

Via Logic takes recruiting fraud seriously. We will never ask candidates for payment, banking information, cryptocurrency, gift cards, or other personal financial information during any stage of the hiring process. All legitimate communication from our team will come directly from authorized Via Logic representatives using official company channels. Due to the rise of fraudulent recruiting activity across the industry, we encourage candidates to use caution if something feels unusual, rushed, or too good to be true. Real adventures should involve solving meaningful challenges -not wiring money to strangers pretending to be recruiters on the internet. If you have concerns about the legitimacy of a communication claiming to represent Via Logic, please verify the information through our official website before sharing personal information or taking further action.

title: Intake Coordinator I or ll
description:

The WMS Intake Coordinator must demonstrate patience with clients, be aware of culturally appropriate behavior and its effects on the responses of clients and be flexible based on the needs of each client.

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:

• High School Diploma (or equivalent) for Level I Assoc. degree in Addiction or related for Level II or equivalent in education/experience

• Plus 3 years’ experience in a medical office, ambulatory care, behavioral health, or similar setting


LICENSES AND CERTIFICATIONS:

• Level II requires current CADC-I or QMHA-I certification

• Must maintain a valid Oregon Driver License or ability to obtain one upon hire and be insurable under the organization’s auto liability coverage policy (minimum 21 years of age and with no Type A violations in the past 3 years, or three (3) or more Type B violations)

• Current BLS/AED


PREFERRED:

• Bilingual in English/Spanish


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

1. Provides initial contact with all referral clients which may include initial interviews with all clients for either self- or professional referrals;

2. Follows up on the referrals in a timely manner to ensure that appropriate care is received, client Is prepared for intake, and understands the WMS process;

11. Attends and participates in daily treatment team meetings to provide updates on incoming patients;

13. Works closely with the billing department and individual counselors to ensure billings and private payments are completed as required;

14. Other related duties as assigned by the Program Supervisor/Director.

title: Archaeologist II (China Lake)
description:
Purpose:

Conduct archaeological monitoring, survey, testing, and data recovery. Conduct research to reconstruct records of past human life and culture from human remains, artifacts, architectural features, and structures recovered through excavation, underwater recovery, or other means of discovery. Non-supervisory. May oversee the day-to-day work of Archaeological Technicians/Crew members.

Duties and Responsibilities:

The Essential Duties and Responsibilities are intended to present a descriptive list of the range of duties performed for this position and are not intended to reflect all duties performed within the job. Other duties may be assigned.

  • Assist senior archaeologists in conducting archaeological and historical site record searches.
  • Perform archival research, field surveys, site mapping, preparing California DPR-523 site forms.
  • Assist in writing reports that record site history, methodology, and artifact analysis results, along with recommendations for conservation and interpreting findings.
  • Study of objects and structures recovered by excavation to identify, date, to authenticate them and interpret their significance.
  • Consult site reports, existing artifacts, and topographic maps to identify archeological sites.
  • Record the precise location and conditions of artifacts uncovered in diggings or surveys, using drawings and photographs as necessary.
  • Create a grid of sites and draw and updates maps of unit profiles, stratum surfaces, features, and findings.
  • Describe artifacts' physical properties or attributes, such as the materials from which artifacts are made and their size, shape, functions, and decoration.
  • Conduct archaeological monitoring, survey, testing and data recovery.
  • Contribute to team efforts during field and lab work.
  • Take the initiative to resolve problems, and assist in creating improved procedures to ensure tasks are completed in the most effective manner.
  • Assist with mapping responsibilities in the field, including collection of GPS data using Trimble units (knowledge of ArcGIS Field Maps is a plus)

Required Qualifications and Experience:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform each essential duty. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Anthropology (or related field) and experience in the field of archaeology.
  • Minimum 1-year experience in archeology/Cultural Resources Management.
  • Must have a valid driver's license
  • Must be able to obtain access to military and other government facilities
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Security Clearance

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Secretary of Interior Standards Professional Qualification Standards Certificate

Physical Demands and Working Conditions:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Employee must maintain a constant state of mental alertness at all times. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Some sedentary work is performed in an office setting, while most work is performed outdoors in rugged terrain, extreme temperature ranges, and often in uninhabited areas.
  • Must be able to walk 8-10 miles a day with a field pack and ample water, over rough terrain in variable weather conditions which include high temperatures in summer months.
  • A portion of the duties require working outdoors under extreme temperature, strenuous physical effort associated with hiking during archaeological reconnaissance and surveys, such as climbing steep slopes, and physical labor such as stooping, bending, carrying loads weighing more than 50 pounds associated with archaeological excavation work.

title: Dental Practice Supervisor
description:
Overview

We are looking for a reliable, hard-working individual to provide supervisory support for our offices located Suffolk. In this Supervisor position, you’ll utilize your team-building and communication skills to the fullest. The right candidate will be organized and have the skills necessary to multitask effectively and efficiently. In addition to exceptional communication and organizational skills, the ideal applicant will lead in a positive, yet productive way. He or she must have the ability to thrive under pressure and work well with others.

This position oversees the daily operations, staffing, and finances of the practice to ensure fundamental systems and protocols are in place and functioning effectively to reach practice goals. This individual is responsible for overseeing the development of the staff, the financial health of the company, as well as community outreach and marketing. Generally, the Team Leader will be responsible for implementing and monitoring the standards and systems as set by the management. Other duties include facilities management and assuring the overall patient satisfaction and goodwill of the practice.

Responsibilities

The following office Supervisor duties are noted; however, other duties may be assigned:

  • Achieves revenue goals by effectively managing patient scheduling, staff productivity, collections and receivables, specialty referral process, and miscellaneous operations expenses.
  • Manages office within budget guidelines to include clerical and auxiliary supply purchases, equipment upgrades, labs and labor costs.
  • Increases and stimulates new patient growth by supporting sales, marketing and promotional programs.
  • Recruits, hires and develops office teams capable of providing best in class patient care.
  • Directly supervises office teams and proactively manages their performance and development including but not limited to performance feedback, appraisals, and corrective actions.
  • Communicates with office teams regularly to ensure they have the information, tools, and support needed to perform their jobs effectively and successfully.
  • Completes administrative tasks, such as flash report review, bank deposits, revenue posting, staff payroll and bonus, accounts receivable reports and invoice processing correctly and within deadline.

title: Associate Content Analyst
description:
Job Description


Clarivate is a global leader committed to innovation and collaboration, offering an environment where you can thrive both professionally and personally. Our Tokyo office, located on the 18th floor, provides breathtaking views of the city, creating an inspiring space for creativity and teamwork. We are seeking an Associate Content Analyst to lead our dynamic team in Penang, Malaysia, embarking on the crucial mission of enhancing the quality and accuracy of Chinese Researcher Profiles. This role is designed for an individual with a strong background in life sciences, extensive experience in academic publishing, and a deep understanding of bibliometrics. Reporting directly to the Team Manager, Scholarly People, the Associate Content Analyst will play a pivotal role in content curation, quality assurance, and stakeholder engagement to ensure our project's success. If you have a proven track record in passion for academic excellence, and fluency in Chinese, we invite you to join us in making a significant impact on the global academic community.

About You:

  • Education: A bachelor or master’s degree in Life Sciences or a related field is essential, reflecting a deep understanding of the subject matter.
  • Experience: 1-2 years of experience in academic publishing or bibliometrics, with a proven track record of leading projects and teams. Prior experience in managing content quality and integrity is crucial.

Skills:

  • Advanced proficiency in the Chinese language for complex editorial tasks is required.
  • Expert knowledge of academic bibliographies, the publication process, and research methodologies in Life Sciences.
  • Exceptional analytical skills and meticulous attention to detail, capable of leading efforts to identify and rectify inaccuracies in academic content.

It would be great if you are...

  • A seasoned expert in academic integrity: With a rich background in enhancing the accuracy and reliability of academic profiles, you're deeply committed to ensuring scholarly contributions are accurately recognized.
  • Analytical and detail-driven: Your extensive experience allows you to identify even the subtlest inconsistencies, ensuring the highest standards of quality in scholarly data.
  • An innovative problem-solver: Beyond identifying issues, you're adept at leading teams to develop creative solutions, streamlining processes to uphold academic records' integrity.
  • A leader in collaboration: You excel in guiding teams, sharing your deep knowledge, fostering a learning environment, and building a positive, productive team culture.
  • A visionary in academic publishing: Keeping abreast of the latest developments in bibliometrics and publishing technology, you're skilled at applying new trends to enhance the team's work.

What will you be doing in this role?

  • Researcher Profile Review & Validation: Review Chinese Researcher Profiles to ensure accurate attribution of publications, affiliations, and author information, maintaining high standards of data quality and integrity.
  • Bibliographic Analysis & Correction: Identify and resolve bibliographic discrepancies, including incorrect authorship claims, publication metadata, and affiliation information, following established guidelines and workflows.
  • Collaboration with Global Teams: Work closely with content operations teams and quality specialists to align on curation practices, share knowledge, and maintain consistent quality standards across researcher profiles.
  • Stakeholder Support: Assist in clarifying profile information and addressing data quality issues through collaboration with internal stakeholders and established support channels.
  • Continuous Improvement & Quality Assurance: Stay current with developments in academic publishing and bibliometrics, applying best practices to improve profile accuracy, workflow efficiency, and overall data quality.

About the Team


Joining our team as a Content Analyst place you at the heart of our ambitious project focused on enhancing the integrity and accuracy of Chinese Researcher Profiles within the Web of Science platform. Our team, an extension of the Content Operations division based in Penang, collaborates closely with over 60 dedicated professionals in India, contributing to a global effort to maintain the highest standards of academic data quality. Internally, we work alongside content editors, specialists, Team manager and Senior Manager while externally, our stakeholders include researchers, academic institutions, and publishing entities. With a project of significant scale, our team size is optimized for agility and effectiveness, allowing for a hands-on approach to problem-solving and innovation. While leveraging a comprehensive suite of tools and technologies tailored to bibliographic and data management, we also enjoy the support of local benefits and a work culture that emphasizes learning, collaboration, and excellence. As part of our team, you'll contribute to a crucial sector of the academic community, ensuring that scholars receive the recognition they deserve for their contributions to the global body of knowledge.


Hours of Work


This is a full-time position, primarily working core business hours in your time zone, with flexibility to adjust to various global time zones as needed.

We comply with applicable laws and regulations governing non-discrimination in all locations.

title: Quality Intern - Summer 2027
description:
• Location: Sterling, Illinois

  • Pay: $28.00 per hour

  • Program start: Tuesday, May 25, 2027, with limited flexibility for academic calendars

  • Duration: 10 weeks, with the possibility of extending up to two additional weeks based on business needs and intern availability

  • Schedule: Full time, 40 hours per week, on site

Help Build Quality into Every Part

As a Quality Intern at MacLean-Fogg, you will connect what you are learning in the classroom with the products and processes behind a manufacturing business. You will work with quality professionals, engineers, and production teams to understand requirements, investigate problems, and help make products and processes more consistent.

You will take ownership of a meaningful project with guidance from an experienced team. Depending on your assignment, you might analyze defect trends, investigate a recurring issue, improve an inspection method, or make quality information easier to use. At the end of the program, you will present your work, findings, and recommendations to facility leadership.

One application connects you with the Quality internship assignments available at this manufacturing facility. Tell us which areas interest you. We will consider your interests, coursework, and experience alongside available projects and business needs.

Quality Areas You Could Explore

Assignments vary by manufacturing facility and may include:

  • Quality Engineering and Problem-Solving: Investigate defects, help identify causes, and support actions that prevent problems from recurring.

  • Measurement, Inspection, and Testing: Learn how teams check product requirements, use measurement tools, and document reliable results.

  • Quality Data and Process Improvement: Analyze trends in defects, scrap, or rework and help teams evaluate opportunities for improvement.

  • Quality Systems and Documentation: Help improve inspection instructions, records, and processes that support consistent work and traceability.

  • Supplier and Customer Quality: Support the review of quality concerns, organize evidence, and help teams track follow-up actions.

You do not need prior experience in these areas. Not every assignment is available at every location.

What You Will Do

  • Learn the products, processes, and quality requirements relevant to your assignment.

  • Gather and organize measurements, observations, and other evidence to understand a problem.

  • Use spreadsheets or other tools to identify patterns and communicate findings.

  • Work with team members to investigate causes and evaluate potential improvements.

  • Support testing or verification of changes under the guidance of qualified team members.

  • Document your work accurately, ask questions when results are unclear, and raise concerns promptly.

  • Follow safety procedures, required training, and instructions for working in manufacturing and laboratory areas.

  • Share project progress, seek feedback, and present your results and recommendations.

What You Bring

  • Enrollment in a bachelor's or master's degree program in engineering, engineering technology, quality technology, materials science, statistics, or a closely related technical field.

  • Interest in manufacturing, product quality, measurement, or process improvement.

  • A thoughtful approach to solving problems and checking your work.

  • Willingness to ask questions, learn from feedback, and work with people in different roles.

  • Ability to organize information and explain your reasoning clearly.

  • Availability for a full-time, on-site summer internship. Limited start-date flexibility may be available for academic calendars.

All college class levels are welcome. Previous internship experience is not required. Coursework, labs, projects, volunteering, student activities, and other jobs can demonstrate your potential.

Helpful, but Not Required

  • A cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher.

  • Coursework or projects involving statistics, measurement, manufacturing, materials, or process improvement.

  • Experience using Excel or another tool to organize and analyze data.

  • Exposure to drawings, measurement tools, inspection methods, or structured problem-solving.

What You Will Gain

  • Ownership of a project with a clear business purpose and defined deliverable.

  • Coaching and feedback from experienced team members.

  • Practical experience working with manufacturing data, products, and processes.

  • Opportunities to collaborate across functions and present your work to leadership.

  • A closer look at potential career paths in Quality and manufacturing.

Housing Assistance

At approved locations, eligible interns may receive a one-time $3,000 taxable housing allowance. To qualify, your available summer residence must be more than 50 miles from the worksite, you must need temporary housing for the internship, and you cannot receive equivalent company-provided housing or relocation support. Payment occurs after the internship begins and required documentation is complete.

title: Senior NPI Supply Chain Engineer, Intelligence Systems
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

The Senior NPI Supply Chain Engineer for Intelligence Systems (internally known as a Senior Product Sourcing Engineer), drives the strategic supply network development and cost management of Anduril’s product hardware across their lifecycles, by collaborating with suppliers and cross-functionally, including folks in engineering, quality, and manufacturing. You will be the end to end owner of supply chain for the Anduril Intelligence & Space business line, responsible for engineering support, vendor onboarding & development, as well sourcing, pricing, and negotiating for the total Bill of Material (BOM).

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Deep dive into your engineering Bill of Material (BOM), working closely with engineering to ensure parts being designed can be sourced & procured at a reasonable target level
  • Conduct supplier selection for a specific product, leveraging our approved supplier list as well as working to onboard unique vendors to support the needs of the Space & Intelligence business team
  • Drive on time delivery utilizing unique solutions to break the mold of traditional Space industry lead-times and supply constraints
  • Partner with strategic suppliers to accelerate product development via activities such as:
    • Concept scoping to quickly solidify requirements
    • Feature trade-off/trade tables
    • Should cost/clean sheet models
    • Joint design development, via clear statements of work
    • Simulation of mechanical & electronics designs
  • Drive the development and consolidation of a manufacturing BOM, working with Engineering, Quality, and Manufacturing, to ramp production internally and with our suppliers with high flexibility
  • Manage total cost of the program, including NPI & mass production throughout NPI
  • Conduct value-stream mapping to optimize supply network lead time and flexibility
  • Complete the BOM risk assessment, include alternate component sourcing, etc.
  • Ensure completion of all component qualifications, ahead of production
  • Reduce complexity: commonality optimization & component/supplier rationalization
  • Lead all cost engineering activities to converge the bottoms-up cost curve to product cost, maximizing the total cost of ownership (TCO) across the product lifecycle
  • Manage ad-hoc cost issues e.g., tariffs / import export cost, and cost inflation
  • Managing supply issues as they arise, ensuring on time delivery at or below target cost

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering or other technical field
  • 8+ years of experience in sourcing engineering, supplier engagement and development, or design of electronics and/or mechanical devices
  • Domain expertise of value/procurement engineering or TCO-related work at the component & product level
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Ability to travel 10% - 40% of the time, variable based on program needs
  • Ability to relocate, if not already local to be onsite in Ashville, OH
  • This role will be based temporarily at Santa Ana, CA for a 3 month training period before transitioning to Ashville, OH

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master's degree or advanced technical degree
  • Deeper experience within:
    • Design & development of electronics and/or mechanical devices
    • Advanced sourcing activities, including stints as commodity/sourcing managers
    • Supplier development (technology, process, supply chain, etc.)
    • Early supplier engagement, ahead of product/engineering requirement realization
  • Familiarity with developing high-tech products in a high-mix, low-volume environment

title: Staff Software Developer (Pre-ID Relo)
description:
Intuit is the global financial technology platform that powers prosperity for the people and communities we serve. Within Workforce Solutions, our Human Capital Management charter builds the products that help small and mid-market businesses hire, pay, and support their people. These are systems customers depend on to run payroll correctly, stay compliant across jurisdictions, and handle the daily work of managing a workforce without friction.

We are hiring a Staff Software Engineer to set technical direction across multiple engineering teams in the HCM charter. This is a charter-wide role. You will not be measured by the features you personally ship, but by the quality of the architecture, standards, and technical decisions that hold across teams, and by the leverage you create for the engineers around you. You will identify the highest-consequence technical problems in HCM, build alignment on how to solve them, and drive them to resolution across organizational boundaries.

The work is architecturally demanding. HCM spans a modern React front end and a large surface of cloud-native backend services, sitting on business logic that must be exactly right: calculation and eligibility rules, auditable compliance behavior across jurisdictions, and integration contracts with adjacent systems across the workforce stack. Much of it is mid-modernization. A significant part of this role is deciding what to rebuild, what to strangle, what to leave alone, and in what order, then making those calls stick.

This role carries explicit accountability for our AI engineering direction. On the product side, you will own the architecture for how HCM builds AI-powered and agentic experiences: the shared patterns, the evaluation infrastructure, the guardrails, and the judgment about where non-deterministic systems belong and where they emphatically do not. On the practice side, you are expected to materially raise how the entire charter engineers with AI, moving the org from individual experimentation to a coherent, high-quality, measurable way of working. We are looking for someone who is already operating at the frontier here and can bring an organization with them.

Staff engineers at Intuit lead without authority. You will influence roadmap, unblock teams, mentor senior engineers, and represent HCM technical strategy to senior engineering and product leadership.


Responsibilities

Technical strategy and architecture

  • Own architectural direction for a significant portion of the HCM charter, spanning multiple teams and services
  • Identify the technical problems that most constrain the charter's velocity, reliability, or customer experience, and drive them to resolution
  • Author and shepherd technical strategy documents and architecture decision records that teams actually build against
  • Define integration contracts and service boundaries across HCM and with adjacent Workforce Solutions platforms
  • Lead modernization and re-platforming strategy: sequencing, migration paths, and risk management, while keeping systems running
  • Make and defend consequential tradeoff decisions with incomplete information, and revisit them openly when the data changes

AI architecture and practice

  • Own the architecture for how HCM builds AI-powered and agentic product capabilities, including shared services, context and retrieval patterns, orchestration, and reuse across teams
  • Establish the evaluation and quality infrastructure for non-deterministic systems: offline and online evals, regression suites, guardrails, fallback behavior, cost and latency budgets, and observability
  • Set the boundary conditions for responsible AI use in compliance-sensitive paths, where a wrong answer has legal and financial consequences for a customer
  • Raise the charter's AI engineering practice measurably: establish patterns, build or select internal tooling, run the forums, and move engineers from ad hoc use to a consistent high-quality workflow
  • Stay ahead of a fast-moving capability landscape and translate genuinely useful advances into concrete architectural and workflow changes, while filtering out what is not yet real

Leverage and influence

  • Multiply the output of engineers across multiple teams through design review, technical mentorship, and unblocking hard problems
  • Mentor senior and staff-track engineers on technical judgment, scope, and influence
  • Raise the engineering bar across teams: design review quality, test strategy, CI/CD, operational readiness, and code health
  • Build alignment across engineering, product, and design leadership without relying on positional authority
  • Represent HCM technical direction in cross-org architecture reviews and to senior leadership
  • Contribute to hiring, leveling calibration, and technical assessment of senior and staff candidates

Operational and delivery accountability

  • Drive systemic improvement in reliability, latency, security posture, and operational toil across the charter, not just within one team
  • Serve as a senior technical escalation point for complex, customer-impacting or cross-team incidents, and drive real root cause resolution
  • Ensure systems meet Intuit standards for security, privacy, data governance, and multi-jurisdiction regulatory compliance
  • Remain hands-on where it creates the most leverage: prototypes, reference implementations, foundational components, and the hardest parts of critical paths

Qualifications

Minimum qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience
  • 8 or more years of professional software engineering experience building and operating production systems at scale
  • Demonstrated experience operating at Staff level or equivalent: setting technical direction that spanned multiple teams and was adopted beyond your immediate scope
  • Deep expertise in distributed systems design, service architecture, API design, and data modeling across relational and non-relational stores
  • Strong full stack range: production depth in a modern backend language such as Java, Kotlin, Go, Python, Ruby or Node.js, with credible working knowledge of a modern front end framework, ideally React
  • Extensive experience with cloud infrastructure such as AWS or GCP, containerization, orchestration, and CI/CD at scale
  • Substantive production experience building AI systems, such as LLM-backed features, retrieval-augmented architectures, or agentic workflows, including responsibility for their quality, evaluation, and operational behavior
  • Demonstrated fluency working AI-first in your own engineering practice, with evidence of having shifted how a team or org works, not just yourself
  • Track record of leading large technical initiatives to completion through influence rather than authority
  • Excellent technical writing, with a portfolio of design documents or strategy documents that drove real organizational decisions
  • Proven ability to mentor and grow senior engineers

Preferred qualifications

  • Domain experience in HR technology, payroll, workforce management, fintech, or another domain where correctness is auditable and financially material
  • Experience architecting rules engines, calculation or ledger-style systems, or complex configurable workflow platforms
  • Experience leading a significant modernization or re-platforming of a live, revenue-bearing legacy system
  • Experience building shared AI platform capabilities or evaluation infrastructure used by multiple product teams
  • Experience defining technical standards or governance adopted across an engineering organization
  • Experience with front end architecture at scale, including design systems, performance, and accessibility
  • Familiarity with data privacy, security, and employment compliance frameworks relevant to employee data, such as SOC 2, GDPR, PIPEDA, CCPA, and jurisdictional employment reporting requirements
  • Experience influencing across a large matrixed organization and multiple time zones
  • Prior experience in a Staff or Principal role at a mid-to-large-size technology company

What we look for

  • Leverage over output. You measure yourself by what the organization ships, not by what you ship
  • Judgment at consequence. You are trusted with the decisions that are expensive to reverse, and you know which ones those are
  • Influence without authority. You bring people to a decision through clarity and credibility rather than escalation
  • Frontier curiosity with engineering rigor. You adopt new capability early and still insist on evidence before it reaches customers
  • Clarity at scale. Your writing changes what an organization does

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit®: Careers | Benefits). Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

Primary Responsibilities
