title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
Staff Software Engineer (fullstack/backend focus, consumer products) - Hybrid, Seattle, WA


RentSpree is looking for a Staff Software Engineer to help lead the development of core consumer and business-facing product experiences. In this role, you’ll be responsible for building and evolving high-impact features end-to-end — from backend APIs to polished interfaces — with an emphasis on delivering fast, intuitive, and reliable experiences for our users.

As a technical leader, you’ll help set the architectural direction, lead complex initiatives from idea to delivery, mentor engineers, and work closely with product, design, and engineering teams and leaders to build intuitive, performant, and reliable experiences for millions of users.

This position is hybrid (2 days/week) in our Seattle office.



What You'll Do

  • Lead end-to-end development of user-facing features across web and backend systems
  • Champion back-end architecture, performance, and accessibility best practices
  • Collaborate with product managers and designers to translate customer needs into thoughtful, scalable solutions
  • Drive technical decision-making and execution on complex initiatives
  • Contribute to and shape our engineering standards, architecture, and tooling
  • Mentor other engineers and contribute to the growth of engineering culture and technical excellence
  • Balance delivery speed and quality, making pragmatic choices around trade-offs
  • Help evolve our backend infrastructure and testing strategies


Our job descriptions evolve with our business needs and priorities. Your role may include other tasks, projects, and team support.



Skills You Bring

  • 8+ years of professional software development experience, including leadership on high-impact projects
  • Proven ability to ship production features end-to-end, including frontend UI, APIs, and backend services
  • Deep expertise in modern back-end technologies (Java or Kotlin with SpringBoot, Node.js, GraphQL/REST APIs, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, cloud platforms)
  • Full-stack fluency, including experience with frontend technologies (React, TypeScript, JavaScript)
  • Proven ability to drive technical direction and architecture in cross-functional settings across multiple teams
  • Strong product sense and empathy for end users
  • Experience mentoring engineers and helping grow technical capabilities on a team
  • Comfortable working in fast-paced, iterative environments with evolving requirements



Bonus Points

  • Experience with large-scale infrastructure
  • Track record of delivering consumer-scale web applications
  • Familiarity with experimentation, analytics, and product iteration cycles
  • Exposure to CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, and production readiness best practices



We are Fueled by our Guiding Principles


How we work and who we are comes down to six guiding principles. These are the principles we hire for and hold ourselves to:

  • Customer obsession: Our customers' needs come first. Not eventually, not when it's convenient. Every decision runs through one question: does this make things better for the people who depend on us?
  • Take action, forge solutions: When there's a problem, we don't wait for permission to solve it. We move with urgency, think past the obvious fix, and build something that holds.
  • Be candid, yet respectful: Say what you think. Name the problem. Challenge the idea. We don't do polite silence, but we also don't do cheap shots. Honest, direct, respectful.
  • Disagree, then commit: The best decisions come from real debate. Say what you think, even if it's uncomfortable. Once we decide, we move together.
  • Be audacious, learn loudly: Take the big swings our mission demands, treat every outcome as impact or a lesson, and share what you learn openly so the whole company grows stronger.
  • Strive for excellence: We don't settle at "done." We ask whether it's right, whether it's better than last time, and whether it's something we'd be proud to put in front of a customer.



AI Compounds the Work


AI is a core skill. The people who thrive here are curious, take ownership, and use AI to compound their thinking, not replace it.



Why Join Us?


The work here is real, the problems are hard, and you'll have teammates who push you to do your best.

  • Compensation. $230-270k base.
  • Equity. Share in what you help build.
  • The team. Talented colleagues who push you and back you up.
  • Room to grow. Coaching, resources, and development beyond the role you start in.
  • Health coverage from day one. Medical, dental, and vision for you and your dependents. HSA/FSA options. Headspace Care+, gym discounts, and more.
  • A real plan for your future. Life and disability coverage, plus a SIMPLE IRA with company match.
  • Flexible vacation. Take the time you need. We trust you to manage it.
  • 11 holidays a year, plus 3 recharge days.
  • Ways to connect. Reimbursed weekly team lunches, game nights, and events. In-person and remote.
  • Recognition. Recognize a peer with Sprees (redeemable for gift cards or donations). Nominate someone for a S.P.R.E.E. Award with a potential spot bonus.
  • The tools to do your best work. Business expense allowance and internet reimbursement.
  • Family support. Parental leave and fertility benefits.
  • Legal and tax help. Legal benefits and tax support through RocketLawyer.
  • Seattle HQ perk. Company-sponsored Orca card for public transit to and from the office.
  • High impact, lean team. Small teams, close to customers, shipping work that matters. Your fingerprints are on the product.



SpreeHours


RentSpree has teams in the US and Bangkok. Collaboration across that distance requires a shared window: Monday-Thursday, 5–7pm PT / 7-9am ICT. How often you're in SpreeHours depends on your role, team, and projects. Any SpreeHours you work, you take back as flex time the same week. Outside of SpreeHours, your schedule is yours.



Ready to Build Something Big?


If you take ownership, move with urgency, and want to work on problems that matter, we'd love to hear from you. You don't need to meet every requirement. If this feels like the right place to do your best work, reach out.



EEO Statement


RentSpree is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other protected characteristic under federal, state, or local law. This applies to all employment practices, including hiring, recruiting, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, leave of absence, compensation, benefits, training, and apprenticeship. Hiring decisions are made on qualifications, merit, and business need.



Don't see the right role, but we're the right company?

We're always on the lookout for talented people. If you don't see a fit today, apply to Future Opportunities and we'll reach out when something matching your background opens up.

title: Head of Planning S&OP
description:
JOB SUMMARY

Join our team at Scientific Protein Laboratories (SPL), a world leader in biosourced pharmaceuticals, located just outside of Madison, Wisconsin in Waunakee! SPL is an innovative biopharmaceutical leader with unique products and services supporting the pharmaceutical industry globally. For over 40 years, SPL specializes in the development and cGMP compliant manufacturing of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs). SPL has an exciting opportunity to join the team as the Head of Planning S&OP.

This position leads Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) and Production and Material Control (PMC) across the SPL site. Supports the Chief Operating Officer (COO) in translating corporate strategy and the Annual Operating Plan (AOP) into SPL-specific strategies and initiatives and driving their implementation; supports annual performance goals setting, cascading, and achievement tracking; assists the COO with periodic performance reporting and special proposals to headquarters; and communicates corporate policies and advances transformation programs within SPL, including management system development, process digitalization, and organizational and talent development.

Responsibilities include:

Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP):

Use sales forecasts and orders as inputs, with fulfillment of sales and customer demand as the primary objective; lead long-term supply-demand balancing across SPL product lines, support market-share and volume-growth targets, and coordinate open-order execution and delivery tracking.

  • Lead the development of the annual and rolling 18-month capacity, output, and raw material charging plan. Build forward-looking capacity models by incorporating production line design capacity, equipment constraints, raw material availability, workforce capacity, maintenance windows, holidays, and other key operational factors, and coordinate cross-functional reviews, periodic reassessments, and timely plan adjustments.
  • Based on AOP, rolling sales forecasts, capacity plans, and raw-material supply plans to design finished-goods inventory levels; set safety-stock and inventory limits; and lead inventory analysis, alerts, and consumption plans for near-expiry or slow-moving stock.
  • Coordinate the S&OP meeting governance, agenda, and material requirements; organize cross-functional analysis of supply and demand, capacity, raw material charging plan, inventory, delivery, and quality risks; review meeting materials and drive follow-through and closure of key decisions and action items.
  • Lead the development and management of standard order lead times; coordinate and resolve cross-functional differences in material preparation, production, testing, and release timelines; review order delivery date assessments and guide the handling and resolution of major delivery schedule issues.
  • Lead the implementation of the make-to-order production model across products; coordinate with Sales to ensure product-specific demand orders are submitted; organize the review of delivery priorities and the corresponding production, release, and delivery schedules; and provide the reviewed plans to Sales
  • Manage end-to-end delivery tracking for product-specific demand orders submitted by Sales and drive the execution and closure of all activities that may impact order delivery. Regularly integrate and analyze sales-production-supply-inventory business data reports for each product and provide issue and risk alerts.

Production Planning and Progress Control (PC):

Use product process routes and order demand as inputs, with timely delivery of each order as the core objective; coordinate order delivery-date feedback; develop and issue master production schedules and monthly production plans for each product line, and track execution.

  • Lead weekly & monthly production plan review and coordination; guide plan adjustments, major exception handling, cross-functional resource coordination, and risk closure to ensure stable production order and achievement of delivery targets.
  • Follow up the progress of finished-goods output testing, and release progress; guide major delivery risk assessments and priority setting; and coordinate cross-functional resources to close order delivery exceptions.

BOM-Based Production Material Planning & Control (MC):

Use production plans as inputs, with material supply assurance and production continuity as the core objective; coordinate BOM master data, material requirement planning, purchase requisition issuance, and tracking through release.

  • Manage BOM master data process, including creation, review, approval, and change management in a timely manner.
  • Lead annual and monthly calculation of BOM-based material requirements and purchase requisition planning; balance production demand, inventory, in-transit quantities, safety stock, and procurement lead times; and guide identification and response to key material supply risks.
  • Lead tracking of arrival, testing, and release progress for key BOM-based materials; guide supply risk assessment and priority setting; coordinate escalation of major material exceptions and supervise issue closure.

System Development and Process Digitalization:

Leverage headquarters’4.0 Product and Service Delivery process architecture as the overarching framework, with a focus on operational efficiency, and tailor it to SPL’s business needs by leading the development and continuous improvement of required SPL-specific processes and digital systems.

  • Lead the design and continuous improvement of S&OP and PMC management systems and processes; guide role-interface definition and key control-point setup; monitor process execution effectiveness and drive issue improvement.
  • Lead the electronic enablement of S&OP and PMC processes and the digitalization of management information; plan business requirements, rules, and implementation priorities; guide system solution review, implementation, and acceptance; coordinate resources and promote system adoption.

Team Management and Talent Development:

Lead departmental organization and talent development, training, AOP, and performance management; guide goal cascading, performance communication and evaluation; coordinate with HR and drive implementation of talent development and performance management.

Job Requirements and Qualifications:

Required:

  • A High School diploma/GED is required.
  • 5+ years of experience in production planning, material control, supply chain planning, S&OP, inventory management, or manufacturing operations, with the ability to organize cross-functional planning communication, data analysis, risk identification, and action-item tracking.

Preferred:

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in Supply Chain, Engineering, or business.
  • ASCM/APICS, CPIM, CSCP, or equivalent supply chain professional certification.
  • 3+ years of experience in S&OP process management, capacity planning, cross-functional supply-demand balancing, production planning governance, inventory strategy, or team/process management.
  • Experience in a GMP (pharmaceutical, biomanufacturing, medical device), food or similarly regulated environment.
  • Familiarity with ERP, MRP, or supply chain planning systems.
  • Experience participating in or implementing digital projects.

WHY JOIN SPL?

Our employees are our success! We recruit motivated people, recognize their contributions, and support their development to reach their full potential.

Perks include: competitive compensation; excellent benefits package - including Medical, Dental and Vision on Day 1; Life and AD&D Insurance, and Short and Long-term Disability; Health and Flexible Saving Account options; Employee Assistance Program, generous vacation; paid Holidays; 401k; advancement opportunities; team-oriented environment; community involvement; company events and more!

SPL is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, creed, disability, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, and any other status protected by applicable local, state or federal law.

title: Leasing Agent
description:
Leasing Agent

St. Anton Multifamily, Inc.


Location: Roseville / Folsom CA

Job Type: Full-Time | Non-Exempt

Pay: $21.00 - $22.00 per hour (DOE)

Reports To: Resident Manager


About the Role

St. Anton Multifamily is seeking a motivated and customer-focused Leasing Agent to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for the full leasing cycle—from engaging prospective residents to successfully executing leases and supporting current residents. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys sales, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and takes pride in delivering excellent customer service while helping maintain high occupancy levels.


What You’ll Do

Leasing & Sales

  • Greet and engage prospective residents via phone, email, online inquiries, and in person
  • Schedule and conduct property tours, showcasing the model and available units
  • Follow up with prospects to convert leads into leases
  • Maintain accurate records of leads, appointments, and leasing activity

Application & Move-In Process

  • Process rental applications and verify required information
  • Explain lease terms, deposits, and move-in requirements
  • Prepare lease agreements and ensure accurate data entry in property systems
  • Coordinate move-in logistics, including inspections, keys, and documentation

Resident Support

  • Provide exceptional service to current and prospective residents
  • Receive and track maintenance requests and follow up on completion
  • Assist with rent collection and delinquency follow-up when needed

Administrative & Reporting

  • Maintain organized resident and applicant files
  • Prepare leasing reports and update unit availability status
  • Support lease renewals and ensure compliance with policies and regulations

Compliance & Market Awareness

  • Ensure full compliance with Fair Housing laws and company policies
  • Stay informed about local market trends and competitor properties

What We’re Looking For

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Previous experience in leasing, sales, or customer service preferred

Skills & Abilities

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • Sales-driven mindset with a customer-first approach
  • Detail-oriented with strong organizational skills
  • Ability to multitask and work both independently and as part of a team
  • Proficiency with computers and office equipment (experience with Yardi is a plus)

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to walk property grounds and tour apartment units
  • Ability to climb stairs and stand/sit for extended periods
  • Ability to lift up to 25 pounds occasionally

Why Join St. Anton Multifamily?

  • Opportunity to grow within a supportive property management team
  • Dynamic work environment with daily interaction and variety
  • Make a direct impact on resident satisfaction and community success

title: Risks, Resilience & Operational Excellence Lead (CH)
description:
Make your mark for patients

We are looking for a Risks, Resilience & Operational Excellence Lead who is strategic, data-driven and demonstrates strong leadership to join our Patient Supply Quality Control - Analytical Operations & Excellence team, based at our UCB campus located in Bulle, Switzerland or Braine-l'Alleud, Belgium.

About the role

You will strengthen the performance, strategic alignment and resilience of our Patient Supply Quality Control organization. You will turn strategic priorities into a clear QC actionable roadmap and build a sustainable performance culture. Through data, structured governance and employee engagement, you will drive operational excellence, oversee risk management and strengthen business continuity while protecting quality, compliance, patient safety and reliable supply.

Who you will work with

You will work closely with the Patient Supply QC Leadership Team and collaborate across Patient Supply, Internal Manufacturing, Quality, Digital, Data, Supply Chain and DT. You will connect different teams and priorities, influence decisions without direct authority and support leaders and operational teams in delivering sustainable and continuous improvements. You will also represent Patient Supply QC within relevant risk, performance and governance communities.

What you will do

  • You will develop and deliver the Patient Supply QC Operational Excellence roadmap.
  • You will lead and coach cross-functional improvement initiatives using Lean, Six Sigma and data-driven problem-solving.
  • You will translate strategic priorities into objectives, roadmaps, milestones and measurable outcomes.
  • You will manage performance frameworks, KPIs, governance reviews and improvement actions.
  • You will oversee the QC risk portfolio, mitigation plans and business-continuity readiness.

Interested? For this role, we are looking for the following education, experience and skills:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in science, engineering, pharmacy, quality, operations, analytics or a related discipline.
  • At least 8 years of experience within a GxP-regulated pharmaceutical, manufacturing or laboratory environment.
  • Strong understanding of pharmaceutical Quality Control and Operational Excellence methodologies.
  • Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certification required; Black Belt preferred.
  • Experience applying Kaizen and Continuous Improvement methodologies.
  • Experience in strategy deployment, performance management, risk management and business-continuity planning.
  • Ability to leverage data to identify improvement opportunities, optimize processes and support evidence-based decision-making.
  • Strong data literacy and ability to collaborate with digital, data and IT teams.
  • Influential and inclusive communicator with strong project leadership skills and excellent English and French.

Are you ready to ‘go beyond’ to create value and make your mark for patients? If this sounds like you, then we would love to hear from you!

About us
UCB is a global biopharmaceutical company, focusing on neurology and immunology. We are over 9.000 people in all four corners of the globe, inspired by patients and driven by science.

Why work with us?
At UCB, we don’t just complete tasks, we create value. We aren’t afraid to push forward, collaborate, and innovate to make our mark for patients. We have a caring, supportive culture where everyone feels included, respected, and has equal opportunities to do their best work. We ‘go beyond’ to create value for our patients, and always with a human focus, whether that’s on our patients, our employees, or our planet. Working for us, you will discover a place where you can grow, and have the freedom to carve your own career path to achieve your full potential.

At UCB, we’ve embraced a hybrid-first approach to work, bringing teams together in local hubs to foster collaborative curiosity. Unless expressly stated in the description or precluded by the nature of the position, roles are hybrid with 40% of your time spent in the office.

UCB is an equal opportunity employer. All employment decisions will be made without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable laws.

Should you require any adjustments to our process to assist you in demonstrating your strengths and capabilities contact us on EMEA-Reasonable_Accommodation@ucb.com. Please note should your enquiry not relate to adjustments; we will not be able to support you through this channel.

title: Senior Staff Software Engineer, Data

    • Strong understanding of data governance, lineage, metadata, privacy, security, access controls, and auditability.
    • Ability to operate effectively at both executive and deeply technical levels, with strong communication, collaboration, and technical leadership skills.
    • Experience supporting AI/ML pipelines, feature engineering, real-time analytics, event-driven architectures, experimentation platforms, or product analytics is a plus.

title: MES Developer
description:
MES Developer

Location: Fort Wayne, Indiana, United States
Industry: Automotive Manufacturing
Role Type: Controls / Automation / MES Engineering

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Controls / MES Engineer to support a ground-up manufacturing automation implementation for a major automotive manufacturer in Warren, Michigan.

This is primarily a new-build development and implementation role, not a sustaining or maintenance position. The engineer will be responsible for designing, programming, integrating, and commissioning controls and manufacturing systems, with a strong focus on Rockwell Studio 5000, Ignition, and PLC-to-MES integration.

The ideal candidate has personally taken automation systems from initial design through commissioning and production launch and can demonstrate hands-on experience developing PLC, HMI/SCADA, and MES functionality rather than only modifying or troubleshooting existing systems.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and develop Allen-Bradley ControlLogix/GuardLogix PLC programs from the ground up using RSLogix 5000 / Studio 5000.

  • Develop PLC architecture including ladder logic, tag structures, UDTs, AOIs, sequencing, diagnostics, alarms, and equipment interfaces.

  • Design and build Ignition HMI/SCADA applications, including screens, tags, scripting, alarms, communications, and system configuration.

  • Develop and implement communication between PLCs and MES systems.

  • Create PLC/MES transaction and handshake logic for manufacturing operations.

  • Support work-order verification, part and serial-number traceability, recipe/model management, production reporting, and pass/fail transactions.

  • Integrate barcode scanners, RFID systems, and other production tracking equipment.

  • Configure and integrate Zebra industrial label printers, including generation and implementation of ZPL code.

  • Develop automated label-printing processes tied to production events, work orders, and cycle completion.

  • Perform controls system startup, debugging, commissioning, FAT/SAT, and production launch activities.

  • Troubleshoot PLC, HMI, MES, networking, and equipment communication issues as needed.

  • Collaborate with manufacturing engineering, IT/MES teams, equipment integrators, and plant personnel throughout implementation.

  • Develop and maintain controls documentation, system architecture, backups, and commissioning records.

Required Qualifications

  • Strong hands-on experience with Allen-Bradley ControlLogix/GuardLogix and Studio 5000 / RSLogix 5000.

  • Demonstrated experience writing new PLC programs for equipment, stations, or production lines from scratch.

  • Hands-on experience with Inductive Automation Ignition.

  • Experience developing Ignition screens, tags, scripting, and/or application architecture.

  • Experience integrating PLCs with MES or manufacturing information systems.

  • Understanding of manufacturing transactions such as work-order validation, traceability, recipes, production reporting, and serial-number tracking.

  • Experience commissioning automated manufacturing equipment.

  • Strong troubleshooting skills across controls hardware, PLC software, industrial networks, and production systems.

  • Experience in automotive or other high-volume discrete manufacturing environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience generating ZPL code and integrating Zebra industrial printers.

  • Experience with barcode and RFID-based production traceability.

  • Ignition Vision and/or Perspective development experience.

  • Industrial networking experience including Ethernet/IP, OPC UA, SQL, or related communication technologies.

  • Experience taking a controls project through the complete lifecycle: design → development → integration → startup → commissioning → production launch.

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Mechatronics, Automation, Industrial Engineering, or a related discipline.

Ideal Candidate

The strongest candidate will have experience building controls systems from the ground up, including PLC programming, Ignition development, and PLC-to-MES integration.

This position is best suited for an engineer who has built and commissioned new manufacturing systems rather than someone whose background is primarily production support or maintenance.

title: Director of Church Partnerships
description:
Mission Statement

To lovingly address the needs of men, women and children experiencing homelessness by sharing the Good News of Salvation and providing a holistic approach to rehabilitation and recovery.

Position Summary

The Director of Church Engagement plays a key role in furthering the Mission’s commitment to excellence in service and Christlike compassion. The Director of Church Partnerships cultivates and strengthens meaningful relationships with current and prospective church partners, inspiring greater engagement with the San Diego Rescue Mission's mission of serving individuals experiencing homelessness. This role strategically guides churches along a pathway of engagement from learning about the Mission, to participating in volunteer and special service opportunities, to becoming faithful, long-term financial partners. Through intentional relationship management, the Director of Church Partnerships retains and grows high-impact church partnerships while representing the Mission's vision, values, and Christ-centered culture with excellence. As a spiritual leader, this position is committed to continual growth as a follower of Christ and invests in the development, coaching, and success of the Church Partnerships Coordinator to maximize the team's effectiveness and impact.

Key Responsibilities

  • Church Relationship Management

  • Cultivate, steward, and grow a portfolio of current and prospective church partners through intentional relationship building.

  • Develop and execute engagement strategies that deepen church involvement with the San Diego Rescue Mission.

  • Conduct regular meetings, presentations, and follow-up with pastors, ministry leaders, church staff and parachurch organizations.

  • Church Engagement & Partnership Development

  • Identify and create meaningful opportunities for churches to serve alongside the Mission through volunteer experiences, events, donation drives, and other strategic initiatives.

  • Guide churches through a progressive engagement pathway from awareness to active participation, to long-term financial partnership.

  • Collaborate with internal departments - Lighthouse, Mission Academy and Community Engagement, to ensure churches have impactful and well-coordinated engagement experiences that also meet the needs of the Mission’s guests and students.

  • Fundraising & Donor Development

  • Retain, steward, and upgrade high-capacity church partners through intentional cultivation and relationship management.

  • Identify opportunities to increase financial investment and secure ongoing support from church partners.

  • Maintain an active caseload, establishing annual goals for engagement, retention, and revenue growth.

  • Strategic Planning & Administration

  • Maintain accurate records of partner engagement, donor activity, and relationship management within the Virtuous (SDRM’s CRM).

  • Track and report key performance metrics related to church engagement, volunteer participation, and financial partnership.

  • Participate in departmental planning, budgeting, and strategic initiatives that advance SDRM’s community engagement goals.

  • Leadership & Team Development

  • Provide leadership, coaching, and ongoing development for the Church Partnerships Coordinator.

  • Establish clear goals, provide regular feedback, and cultivate professional and spiritual growth within the team.

  • Foster a collaborative, service-oriented culture that reflects the Mission's values.

  • Spiritual Leadership

  • Demonstrate a vibrant and growing personal relationship with Jesus Christ through consistent spiritual disciplines and Christlike character.

  • Integrate biblical principles into leadership, decision-making, and relationship building.

  • Pray regularly for church partners, team members, donors, volunteers, and those served by the Mission.

  • Model the Mission's Christian values in all interactions and responsibilities.

  • Mission Representative

  • Serve as an ambassador of the San Diego Rescue Mission by communicating its mission, vision, values, and impact with authenticity and excellence.

  • Represent the organization at church services, conferences, community events, and networking opportunities.

  • Share compelling stories of transformation that inspire churches toward greater partnership.

  • Support and participate in ministry-wide activities and chapels as applicable.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally to uphold trauma-informed practices and ensure client dignity.

Staff Expectations

As a representative of San Diego Rescue Mission, all employees are expected to:

  • Adhere to the Statement of Faith, upholding biblical principles in all aspects of work and life.

  • Be prepared to share the hope you have in Christ. As a representative of Christ, be ready to gently and respectfully share the Good News of Jesus Christ at all times.

  • Live out the Mission, Vision, and Values of the SDRM by safeguarding the Mission, pursuing the Vision, and reflecting our core values—Faith, Compassion, Excellence, Integrity, and Fun—in both your personal and public life. Remain focused on serving, demonstrating a deep desire to see God transform the lives of those experiencing homelessness.

  • Intentionally spend time in God’s Word, prayer, staying rooted in a biblical community (local church, ministry, small group) to deepen your relationship with Christ.

  • Model servant leadership in all interactions, encourage and support SDRM staff in their walk with Christ, putting the needs of others before yourself.

  • Foster a coachable, approachable, and humble spirit, remaining open to feedback, growth, and guidance.

title: Academic Advisor
description:
Summary of Position

The Academic Advisor position works with traditional and adult undergraduate students. The position provides culturally competent advising to Augsburg’s diverse undergraduate students, with a full range of support including orientation, academic program planning, course selection, and registration. The position works to monitor student progress and suggests and connects students with appropriate student support team members when students encounter academic difficulties, working holistically with students on issues of the hidden curriculum and navigating college systems. The person will coordinate with other University departments regarding programs that support student progress.

The Academic Advisor also works with the student information system and various data files and sources, and prepares a wide variety of reports using multiple data sources. The position keeps abreast of University policies and procedures, and rules and regulations to assist students in meeting academic requirements. The position does special projects as assigned.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Provides advising for undergraduate students, prospective students, and transfer students, including but not limited to: assisting students on academic, career and personal issues; identifying the educational and career options appropriate for each student and assisting with the analysis of each option, including possible outcomes and their implications.
  • Assists students and faculty advisors with registration and scheduling issues, drop/add, change of registration and registration holds, and general advising questions.
  • Provides guidance in course selection in keeping with the student's interests, goals and abilities. Provides coordination and support to ensure student progress toward degree completion and graduation.
  • Supports the implementation and management of technology tools that support enhanced academic advising and student success strategies.
  • Keep abreast of higher education policies, procedures, rules, and regulations to assist students in meeting academic requirements.
  • Responds to inquiries, investigates, and resolves problems related to course registration, course selection and scheduling, academic success.
  • Interprets and explains college and university policies and procedures to parents and prospective students as well as to current students and faculty.
  • In conjunction with the University and the Director of Academic Advising, coordinates the department's participation in a variety of special admissions and advising events.

Additional Responsibilities

  • When staff members are out of the office or away from their desk, the team members share responsibility for their colleague's workload. This includes but is not limited to front desk coverage, responding to e-mails and phone calls, and administering assessment tests.
  • Collaborate with faculty and staff from various departments in: committee work, staff meetings, and consultation with individual academic departments and support services (Trio-SSS, CLASS, Counseling, Student Support Directors, Athletics, Center for Service Work and Learning, Residence Life, Information Technology, etc.)
  • Initiate and maintain connections with professional associations and colleagues, including: Minnesota Private College Advising Network and National Academic Advising Association.
  • Special projects as assigned.
  • All other duties as apparent or assigned by supervisor(s).

Work Environment and Physical Demands

  • Typical work environment is an office. (To ensure student confidentiality, Gage Center conference rooms are utilized when office partners have concurrent appointments).
  • Sedentary work for long periods of time.
  • Regular computer and phone use.
  • Periods of intense work environment throughout the academic year.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Counseling, Psychology, College Administration, or other closely related field.
  • Three (3) years of relevant professional work experience.
  • Knowledge of counseling theories and student development required.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities

  • Demonstrated ability to work cross-culturally with students, faculty, and staff.
  • Ability to communicate effectively orally and in writing.
  • Ability to work effectively and collaboratively in a diverse work environment.
  • Ability to be attentive to details, be accurate, be precise.
  • Ability to lead/teach; work in a team environment; and work independently with little supervision.
  • Ability to reason/analyze; maintain confidentiality; and demonstrate patience, understanding.
  • Ability to show initiative; organize workflow; manage multiple projects; and handle frequent interruptions.

Compensation and Benefits at Augsburg

  • The compensation range is $47,000 - $53,000 per year, DOQ.

Augsburg University offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards program including:

  • Medical, dental and vision coverage
  • A generous 403(b) matching program with an employer contributions of up to 8% upon eligibility
  • Up to 100% tuition remission for employees, spouses and dependents, and participation in the Tuition Exchange program with colleges and universities throughout the US
  • Generous paid time-off, including 14 paid holidays, 12 sick days, 2 community service days, and vacation of up to 22 days per year immediately upon hire
  • Employer-paid STD, LTD and life insurance
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for all employees

title: Senior Software Engineer, Promotions
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Software Engineer, Promotions based in United States .

This is a senior engineering opportunity focused on building reliable, scalable technology that powers personalized promotional experiences. You will work on the promotions engine and the services that enable marketing teams to create compelling offers and deliver them across digital products. The role combines hands-on development, system architecture, performance optimization, and technical problem-solving. You will design APIs and services while integrating with internal and third-party platforms across multiple client experiences. Production reliability, scalability, and operational excellence are central to the work. You will also collaborate across teams and mentor engineers while helping shape solutions for complex technical challenges.

Accountabilities:

  • Design, scale, and performance-tune GraphQL APIs, low-latency gRPC services, and SQL queries powering the promotions engine.
  • Own technical challenges with significant scope and complexity, developing solution proposals and presenting them to leadership and partner teams for feedback.
  • Design, architect, and deliver new features end-to-end within a collaborative Agile/Scrum environment.
  • Identify production bottlenecks, scalability constraints, and areas of technical risk, then drive improvements to strengthen platform performance and reliability.
  • Establish and refine monitoring and alerting through Datadog for the systems under your ownership.
  • Investigate production performance issues and implement improvements that address CPU hotspots, latency regressions, and other high-throughput service challenges.
  • Participate in on-call rotations and take ownership of production release cycles from end to end.
  • Mentor engineers across teams through technical specifications, pairing, code reviews, and knowledge sharing.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders and engineering teams to deliver reliable promotional capabilities and continuously improve the underlying platform.

    • Requirements:

    • At least 5 years of professional software engineering experience.
    • Strong computer science fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, distributed systems, and software design.
    • Proven experience working with production systems at scale, including load testing, tracing, performance analysis, and optimization.
    • Experience investigating and remediating production performance regressions, particularly CPU and latency issues in high-throughput services.
    • Experience with on-call rotations for production services and end-to-end ownership of release cycles.
    • Strong understanding of clean code architecture and software craftsmanship.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience creating technical specifications, runbooks, and cross-team design documentation.
    • Experience with modern web frameworks and API development, such as Phoenix, Ruby on Rails, FastAPI, Laravel, or Node.js.
    • At least 2 years of experience designing and evolving GraphQL schemas for product surfaces used across multiple clients, including iOS, Android, and web.
    • Experience building and integrating multi-client or white-label platforms, including geo-based routing and client-specific configuration.
    • Strong knowledge of relational databases, particularly PostgreSQL and MySQL.
    • Experience with Kubernetes and operating services in containerized environments.
    • Comfortable working with terminal-based tools, Git, GitHub or similar platforms, and modern development environments.
    • Experience with testing frameworks such as ExUnit, RSpec, Jest, pytest, or equivalent.
    • Experience with background job processing technologies such as Oban, Exq, Sidekiq, Celery, or Beanstalk.
    • Experience with asynchronous event-handling infrastructure such as Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, AWS SQS/SNS, or Google Cloud Pub/Sub.
    • Experience building applications in Elixir is a plus.
    • Familiarity with hexagonal architecture, Domain-Driven Development, open-source contributions, or startup environments is desirable.
    • Passion for sports and/or esports is a plus.

      • Benefits:

      • Published salary range of $145,000–$193,000 USD annually.
      • Competitive compensation package.
      • Potential bonus eligibility for non-sales positions.
      • Comprehensive benefits for eligible employees.
      • Education and conference reimbursement.
      • Opportunities for career progression.
      • Opportunities to mentor and support other engineers.
      • Remote work environment.
      • Fun and relaxed working environment.

title: Mortgage Loan Assistant
description:

The Mortgage Loan Assistant serves as the primary customer contact throughout the mortgage process, from application through closing. This role coordinates all aspects of the loan file, ensures compliance with lending requirements, and acts as the central point of communication between borrowers, Mortgage Loan Officers (MLOs), real estate professionals, attorneys, appraisers, and underwriting teams.


What You'll Do

  • Complete and review loan applications with borrowers and MLOs.
  • Explain mortgage process, timelines, and milestones to customers.
  • Order and track appraisals, title work, flood determinations, and credit reports.
  • Prepare and deliver required disclosures and documentation.
  • Collect and review documents needed for underwriting.
  • Coordinate commitment letters and satisfy loan conditions.
  • Ensure appraisal and Closing Disclosure delivery within required timelines.
  • Schedule closings and coordinate with all parties involved.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact throughout the mortgage process.
  • Support a smooth customer experience from application to closing.

What You Bring

  • Mortgage loan processing experience.
  • Mortgage loan assistant, underwriting, or closing experience.
  • Working knowledge of the full mortgage lifecycle, including:
    • Origination
    • Processing
    • Underwriting
    • Pricing
    • Loan servicing
  • Experience with Mortgage Loan Origination Systems (LOS).

Preferred Knowledge

  • Freddie Mac guidelines
  • FHA programs
  • VA programs
  • Rural Development loans
  • NHHFA/VHFA programs
  • Mortgage compliance and disclosure requirements

Key Skills

  • Strong customer service and communication skills
  • Attention to detail and organization
  • Ability to manage multiple files and deadlines
  • Confidentiality and professionalism
  • Strong computer and technology skills
  • Self-motivated and able to work independently

title: Legal Specialist Prosecutor's Office
description:

Management reserves the rights to add, modify, change, or rescind the work assignments of different positions and to make reasonable accommodations so that qualified employees can perform the essential functions of the job.

1. Processes citations for defendants, in-custody and non-in-custody, for court appearance or action. Creates and builds files; retrieves reports and history for file development purposes.

lift, carry, push, and pull materials and objects weighing up to 20 pounds.

title: Supply Chain Intern - Summer 2027
description:
• Location: Plymouth, MI

  • Pay: $26.00 per hour

  • Program start: Tuesday, May 25, 2027, with limited flexibility for academic calendars

  • Duration: 10 weeks, with the possibility of extending up to two additional weeks based on business needs and intern availability

  • Schedule: Full time, 40 hours per week, on site

Help Connect Materials, People, and Plans

As a Supply Chain Intern at MacLean-Fogg, you will connect classroom learning with the work of getting materials where they are needed, when they are needed. You will work with supply chain professionals and teams across the manufacturing facility to understand demand, supply, inventory, and the decisions that keep work moving.

You will take ownership of a meaningful project with guidance from an experienced team. Depending on your assignment, you might investigate an inventory discrepancy, analyze supplier delivery trends, improve a planning report, or help make a recurring process more reliable. At the end of the program, you will present your work, findings, and recommendations to facility leadership.

One application connects you with the Supply Chain internship assignments available at this location. Tell us which areas interest you. We will consider your interests, coursework, and experience alongside available projects and business needs.

Supply Chain Areas You Could Explore

Assignments vary by location and may include:

  • Purchasing and Supplier Management: Help organize purchasing information, compare supplier performance, and support follow-up on materials or services.

  • Production and Materials Planning: Learn how teams connect customer demand, available materials, and production schedules.

  • Inventory and Materials Management: Help analyze inventory records, investigate discrepancies, and improve visibility of material availability.

  • Logistics and Transportation: Support analysis of shipping, receiving, delivery, or freight information to improve reliability and efficiency.

  • Supply Chain Data and Process Improvement: Use data to understand recurring issues and help teams improve reports, handoffs, or workflows.

You do not need prior experience in these areas. Not every assignment is available at every location.

What You Will Do

  • Learn the products, materials, systems, and processes relevant to your assignment.

  • Gather and organize purchasing, inventory, planning, or delivery information and check its accuracy.

  • Use spreadsheets or other tools to identify patterns, compare options, and communicate findings.

  • Work with purchasing, scheduling, operations, quality, and other teams to understand practical needs.

  • Support follow-up on open actions and help keep stakeholders informed of changes or risks.

  • Help document processes and evaluate improvements under the guidance of experienced team members.

  • Handle supplier, pricing, and business information carefully.

  • Follow required training and safety procedures when working in manufacturing, shipping, or receiving areas.

  • Share project progress, seek feedback, and present your results and recommendations.

What You Bring

  • Enrollment in a bachelor's or master's degree program in supply chain management, logistics, operations management, business analytics, business administration, industrial engineering, or a closely related field.

  • Interest in how purchasing, planning, inventory, and logistics support a manufacturing business.

  • A thoughtful approach to solving problems and checking your work.

  • Willingness to ask questions, learn from feedback, and work with people in different roles.

  • Ability to organize information and explain your reasoning clearly.

  • Availability for a full-time, on-site summer internship. Limited start-date flexibility may be available for academic calendars.

All college class levels are welcome. Previous internship experience is not required. Coursework, projects, volunteering, student activities, and other jobs can demonstrate your potential.

Helpful, but Not Required

  • A cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher.

  • Coursework or projects involving supply chain, operations, statistics, business analytics, or process improvement.

  • Experience using Excel or another tool to organize and analyze data.

  • Experience coordinating a project, tracking deadlines, or improving a process.

What You Will Gain

  • Ownership of a project with a clear business purpose and defined deliverable.

  • Coaching and feedback from experienced team members.

  • Practical experience connecting purchasing, planning, inventory, and logistics with manufacturing work.

  • Opportunities to collaborate across functions and present your work to leadership.

  • A closer look at potential career paths in Supply Chain.

Housing Assistance

At approved locations, eligible interns may receive a one-time $3,000 taxable housing allowance. To qualify, your available summer residence must be more than 50 miles from the worksite, you must need temporary housing for the internship, and you cannot receive equivalent company-provided housing or relocation support. Payment occurs after the internship begins and required documentation is complete.

Physical Requirements and Work Environment

The physical demands below represent those required to perform the essential functions of this position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Sit at a workstation and use a computer for extended periods.

  • Move throughout manufacturing areas to observe equipment, processes, and production activities.

  • Occasionally lift and carry tools, samples, or parts weighing up to 30 pounds.

  • Occasionally bend, stoop, kneel, and reach when observing equipment or components.

  • Review drawings, gauges, measurement equipment, and other visual information.

  • Wear required personal protective equipment, which may include safety glasses, hearing protection, and safety footwear.

  • Work in office and manufacturing environments where noise, temperature variation, and airborne particulates may be present.

What to Expect After Applying

Our hiring process includes an application, Criteria assessments, application and assessment review, a recruiter screen, and a 45-minute interview with the hiring team. Candidates selected for an offer receive a conditional offer followed by required pre-employment screening before hire.

This position requires a pre-employment drug screen after a conditional offer. A criminal background check may also be required, depending on the role. Screening and employment decisions are administered consistent with applicable law.

About MacLean-Fogg

MacLean-Fogg is a fourth-generation, family-owned American manufacturing company headquartered in Mundelein, Illinois. Founded in 1925, we design and manufacture engineered components and solutions for automotive and industrial markets.

Our portfolio includes MacLean-Fogg Component Solutions, OMCO, Mallard Manufacturing, and Threadstrong. Across our companies, we share a commitment to Safety, Integrity, People, Excellence, and Stewardship while investing in our people, manufacturing capabilities, customers, and communities.

Equal Employment Opportunity and Accommodations

MacLean-Fogg and its affiliated companies are equal opportunity employers. We provide equal employment opportunities to qualified applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, military or veteran status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

If you need a reasonable accommodation to apply, complete an assessment, or participate in the hiring process, contact careers@macleanfogg.com.

Hos Olivia Danmark arbejder vi hver dag for at levere omsorg af høj kvalitet med fokus på faglighed, viden og dedikation.

title: Quality Intern - Summer 2027
description:
• Location: Farmington Hills, Michigan

  • Pay: $28.00 per hour

  • Program start: Tuesday, May 25, 2027, with limited flexibility for academic calendars

  • Duration: 10 weeks, with the possibility of extending up to two additional weeks based on business needs and intern availability

  • Schedule: Full time, 40 hours per week, on site

Help Build Quality into Every Part

As a Quality Intern at MacLean-Fogg, you will connect what you are learning in the classroom with the products and processes behind a manufacturing business. You will work with quality professionals, engineers, and production teams to understand requirements, investigate problems, and help make products and processes more consistent.

You will take ownership of a meaningful project with guidance from an experienced team. Depending on your assignment, you might analyze defect trends, investigate a recurring issue, improve an inspection method, or make quality information easier to use. At the end of the program, you will present your work, findings, and recommendations to facility leadership.

One application connects you with the Quality internship assignments available at this manufacturing facility. Tell us which areas interest you. We will consider your interests, coursework, and experience alongside available projects and business needs.

Quality Areas You Could Explore

Assignments vary by manufacturing facility and may include:

  • Quality Engineering and Problem-Solving: Investigate defects, help identify causes, and support actions that prevent problems from recurring.

  • Measurement, Inspection, and Testing: Learn how teams check product requirements, use measurement tools, and document reliable results.

  • Quality Data and Process Improvement: Analyze trends in defects, scrap, or rework and help teams evaluate opportunities for improvement.

  • Quality Systems and Documentation: Help improve inspection instructions, records, and processes that support consistent work and traceability.

  • Supplier and Customer Quality: Support the review of quality concerns, organize evidence, and help teams track follow-up actions.

You do not need prior experience in these areas. Not every assignment is available at every location.

What You Will Do

  • Learn the products, processes, and quality requirements relevant to your assignment.

  • Gather and organize measurements, observations, and other evidence to understand a problem.

  • Use spreadsheets or other tools to identify patterns and communicate findings.

  • Work with team members to investigate causes and evaluate potential improvements.

  • Support testing or verification of changes under the guidance of qualified team members.

  • Document your work accurately, ask questions when results are unclear, and raise concerns promptly.

  • Follow safety procedures, required training, and instructions for working in manufacturing and laboratory areas.

  • Share project progress, seek feedback, and present your results and recommendations.

What You Bring

  • Enrollment in a bachelor's or master's degree program in engineering, engineering technology, quality technology, materials science, statistics, or a closely related technical field.

  • Interest in manufacturing, product quality, measurement, or process improvement.

  • A thoughtful approach to solving problems and checking your work.

  • Willingness to ask questions, learn from feedback, and work with people in different roles.

  • Ability to organize information and explain your reasoning clearly.

  • Availability for a full-time, on-site summer internship. Limited start-date flexibility may be available for academic calendars.

All college class levels are welcome. Previous internship experience is not required. Coursework, labs, projects, volunteering, student activities, and other jobs can demonstrate your potential.

Helpful, but Not Required

  • A cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher.

  • Coursework or projects involving statistics, measurement, manufacturing, materials, or process improvement.

  • Experience using Excel or another tool to organize and analyze data.

  • Exposure to drawings, measurement tools, inspection methods, or structured problem-solving.

What You Will Gain

  • Ownership of a project with a clear business purpose and defined deliverable.

  • Coaching and feedback from experienced team members.

  • Practical experience working with manufacturing data, products, and processes.

  • Opportunities to collaborate across functions and present your work to leadership.

  • A closer look at potential career paths in Quality and manufacturing.

Physical Requirements and Work Environment

The physical demands below represent those required to perform the essential functions of this position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Sit at a workstation and use a computer for extended periods.

  • Move throughout manufacturing areas to observe equipment, processes, and production activities.

  • Occasionally lift and carry tools, samples, or parts weighing up to 30 pounds.

  • Occasionally bend, stoop, kneel, and reach when observing equipment or components.

  • Review drawings, gauges, measurement equipment, and other visual information.

  • Wear required personal protective equipment, which may include safety glasses, hearing protection, and safety footwear.

  • Work in office and manufacturing environments where noise, temperature variation, and airborne particulates may be present.

What to Expect After Applying

Our hiring process includes an application, Criteria assessments, application and assessment review, a recruiter screen, and a 45-minute interview with the hiring team. Candidates selected for an offer receive a conditional offer followed by required pre-employment screening before hire.

This position requires a pre-employment drug screen after a conditional offer. A criminal background check may also be required, depending on the role. Screening and employment decisions are administered consistent with applicable law.

About MacLean-Fogg

MacLean-Fogg is a fourth-generation, family-owned American manufacturing company headquartered in Mundelein, Illinois. Founded in 1925, we design and manufacture engineered components and solutions for automotive and industrial markets.

Our portfolio includes MacLean-Fogg Component Solutions, OMCO, Mallard Manufacturing, and Threadstrong. Across our companies, we share a commitment to Safety, Integrity, People, Excellence, and Stewardship while investing in our people, manufacturing capabilities, customers, and communities.

We provide equal employment opportunities to qualified applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, military or veteran status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

You’ll work closely with architects, engineers, and cross-functional teams to ensure solutions are scoped, delivered, and aligned with business objectives. title: Credit Counselor (Collections Specialist) - Espanola/ Santa Fe, NM
description:
The Credit Counselor I works with members to resolve delinquent loan accounts by evaluating financial situations, negotiating repayment solutions, and providing financial guidance. This role supports loss prevention efforts, ensures compliance with collection policies and regulations, maintains accurate account documentation, and delivers exceptional member service while helping members achieve financial stability.


Join Our Team at Del Norte Credit Union!
We’re more than a financial institution, we’re a community. Guided by our mission of Improving Lives and vision of being Authentically New Mexico, we embrace Del Norteño Pride, reflecting our commitment to community, culture, and connection. Proudly recognized as a Platinum-Level Family Friendly Business, we value People Focus, Collaboration, and Continuous Learning.


Location:

Operations Center located in Espanola, NM. Hybrid work is possible with approval from supervisor and will be subject to change based on the needs of the organization or department.


Essential Functions & Responsibilities:

Level I:

  • Contact delinquent members by phone, mail, and other approved methods to resolve past-due loan accounts and minimize delinquency losses.
  • Analyze members' financial situations, credit reports, and repayment capacity to recommend appropriate solutions and repayment strategies.
  • Negotiate payment arrangements, loan extensions, and debt resolution plans that help members restore accounts to good standing.
  • Process member requests, payments, loan extensions, insurance claims, disability claims, credit life claims, and total loss claims in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Utilize collection systems, core processing platforms, and skip-tracing tools to locate members, manage accounts, and document collection activities.
  • Maintain accurate, detailed, and compliant records of all member interactions, collection efforts, and account resolutions.
  • Educate members on financial responsibilities, account terms, and available credit union products and services that support financial well-being.
  • Monitor and identify delinquency trends, providing feedback and recommendations to management to improve loan performance and mitigate risk.
  • Collaborate with team members and internal departments to deliver exceptional member service, achieve departmental goals, and support the credit union's mission.
  • Ensure compliance with all collection laws, regulations, credit union policies, security procedures, and confidentiality standards.

Level II ( to include Level I requirements):

  • Accurately update credit bureau reporting when applicable
  • Recommends accounts for further action including workouts, legal and charge offs.
  • Maintains a working knowledge of Chapter 7 and 13 Bankruptcies and processes basic bankruptcy claims.
  • Maintain a working knowledge of Repossessions up to and including Liquidation.

People Focus - Level 2 (Core)

Collaborating with Others - Level 2 (Core)

Continuous Learning - Level 2 (Core)

Information Management - Level 2 (Job-specific)

Professionalism - Level 2 (Job-specific)

Fostering Communication - Level 2 (Job-specific)

Credit Management - Level 1 (Job-specific)

Analytical Thinking - Level 1 (Job-specific)

Level I: $19.80 – $24.76 per hour

Level II: $22.08 – $27.60 per hour

New hires are typically brought in between the range minimum and maximum based on qualifications, internal equity, and budget

title: Outside Grease Technician (CDL A) Day Shift
description:
At Wind River Environmental, we keep businesses running by providing essential environmental services to restaurants, supermarkets, and commercial facilities across the region. We’re looking for hardworking, safety-focused CDL drivers who don’t mind getting their hands dirty and take pride in solving problems out in the field. If you enjoy independent work, staying active, and being part of a team that values safety, reliability, and growth opportunities, this could be a great fit for you.


The base pay range for this role is estimated to be $26.00 - $29,00 at the time of posting. Final compensation will be determined by various factors such as work location, education, experience, knowledge, and skills.


What You’ll Do

As an Outside Grease Technician, you’ll service commercial grease trap systems for major restaurant and grocery accounts. Every day is different — from locating and uncovering grease traps to pumping systems, troubleshooting issues, and helping customers keep their operations running smoothly.


Responsibilities include:

  • Safely operate vacuum trucks and equipment at customer locations
  • Drive to and from job sites while following all DOT and traffic regulations
  • Pump, clean, and maintain commercial grease trap systems
  • Inspect grease traps for buildup, damage, or safety concerns
  • Troubleshoot issues and communicate findings with customers and management
  • Prepare trucks, hoses, tools, and equipment before service calls
  • Complete service paperwork and reports accurately and on time
  • Respond to emergency or after-hours service calls when needed
  • Follow all Wind River Environmental safety and service protocols
  • Wear required PPE and work safely at all times
  • Participate in on-call rotations, overtime, weekends, and holiday work as needed

What We’re Looking For

  • Valid CDL Class A or B license with an acceptable driving record (Class A prefer no restrictions)
  • Minimum 1 year of commercial driving experience (after CDL school)
  • Ability to pass DOT drug screening, medical certification, road test, and physical exam
  • Comfortable working independently and outdoors in all weather conditions
  • Strong communication and customer service skills
  • Basic computer and mobile device skills
  • Ability to read maps, safety documents, and service instructions
  • High school diploma or GED required

Physical & Work Environment


This is a hands-on, physical role. Candidates must be comfortable:

  • Working outdoors in varying weather conditions
  • Lifting, bending, climbing, and working around grease and wastewater systems
  • Working around truck equipment, hoses, pumps, noise, and non-hazardous fumes
  • Working night shifts and extended hours when needed

Pay & Benefits


We offer a strong benefits package designed to support you on and off the job:

  • Competitive hourly pay + overtime opportunities
  • Quarterly safety bonus program
  • Step Program advancement opportunities
  • Company-paid Smith Systems defensive driving training
  • Company-paid DOT medical card renewals
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Employer-paid life insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Paid holidays and generous PTO package
  • Company-paid uniforms
  • Annual safety boot stipend
  • Employee discounts on services in your area
  • Career growth opportunities within a growing company

Why Wind River Environmental?

At Wind River Environmental, our people are the backbone of what we do. We invest in training, safety, and career growth while building a culture where hard work is recognized and teamwork matters.


Wind River Environmental is a leading provider of non-hazardous liquid waste services throughout the East Coast. We provide essential environmental services to commercial, residential, and municipal customers with a strong focus on safety, reliability, and customer service.

title: AOD Counselor
description:
SUMMARY

Under the direct supervision of the Administrator, the Facility Manager/ Registered Counselor is responsible for the day to day operations of the facility. This includes the direct care and supervision of the youth, completion of all scheduled AOD groups and services under their scope of practice, documentation of services in county electronic health record, supervision of assigned residential counselors, implementation of the behavior modification program, and daily documentation regarding youth behaviors. The Facility Manager/ Registered Counselor ensures the facility complies with Community Care Licensing, Title 22 Regulations, Paradise Oaks Youth Services (POYS) policies & procedures, and other applicable regulations and procedures.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The incumbent will perform, or cause to have performed, the following items:

1. Management of group home environment and physical plant during assigned shifts.

2. Direct supervision of residential counselors and program activities including housekeeping, personal hygiene, recreation, mealtime, visiting, etc. Includes enforcement of all program rules and expectations.

3. In coordination with the therapist, completion of ASAM assessments as appropriate

4. Conduct all scheduled AOD services assigned and document services in youths’ electronic health record

5. Conduct employee orientations and/or in-service training as requested.

6. Compliance with the program statement, Paradise Oaks Youth Services, the State of California Department of Social Services and other applicable regulations and procedures.

7. Review of youth packets with other team members and recommendation of appropriate actions to higher authority.

9. Establishment and/or following of prescribed procedures to insure that clients receive necessary support, supervision, clinical, and administrative services to provide quality therapeutic experiences. 10. Dispensing of medication in a timely and accurate fashion in accordance with doctor's orders, nursing training, and per POYS’s Medication Policy.

11. Implementation of residents' individual treatment plans.

13. May perform minor household maintenance functions and/or submit work requests for maintenance department actions.

14. Responsible for written and oral evaluations and reviews of all assigned subordinate employees.

15. Completion of other duties consistent with the above as may be periodically assigned by the supervisor.

title: Data Portfolio Lead (US)
description:
Make your mark for patients

Data Portfolio Lead

We are looking for a Data Portfolio Lead who is curious, collaborative, and outcome-oriented to join us in our Transformation initiative program, Ruby, based in either our United States office, in Europe: in our headquarters in Belgium or in our UK based office located in Slough.

About the role

You will improve critical business decisions and processes across an assigned portfolio by ensuring the right data is available, connected, and usable. You will identify high-value business questions, translate them into integrated data products, and coordinate contributions across data domains. You will also define the shared business meaning and context of these products, helping ensure they are trusted, reusable, governed, and ready to support analytics and artificial intelligence. Your focus will be to turn important business questions into trusted data products and measurable business outcomes.

You will be working in a team that connects business, data, analytics, artificial intelligence, and technology expertise. You will partner with business and process owners, business analysts, data product leads, data operations, data governance teams, subject matter experts, and digital technology teams. Together, you will align reusable data capabilities with portfolio priorities and deliver scalable solutions that support decision-making and business value.

  • Translate business questions into prioritized data product opportunities, clear requirements, acceptance criteria, success measures, and measurable outcomes.

  • Monitor adoption, usage, and business impact, using feedback and measurement to drive continuous improvement and value realization.

Interested? For this role we're looking for the following education, experience and skills

  • Bachelor's degree in business, data, analytics, life sciences, information management, technology, or a related field; an advanced degree is preferred.
  • Experience connecting business strategy, process improvement, data, analytics, and artificial intelligence to measurable business outcomes.
  • Experience working across business functions and data domains, translating business questions into data, analytical, and technology requirements.
  • Experience combining multiple domain data products into fit-for-purpose solutions that answer specific business questions.
  • Experience defining business concepts, shared meaning, relationships, or information models for cross-domain data products.
  • Experience partnering with business analysts on specifications, acceptance criteria, testing, validation, and success measures.
  • Strong business acumen, data fluency, systems thinking, problem-solving, stakeholder influence, and facilitation skills.
  • Experience in pharmaceutical, healthcare, or life sciences environments is preferred, with a collaborative and accountable approach across organizational boundaries.
